part_metadata.name: Endothelium
part_metadata.description: Continuous thin cellular lining of the representative vein, continuous with the endothelial covering at valve roots. Surface cells and relief are enlarged for teaching; they do not measure endothelial thickness or permeability.

part_metadata.name: Subendothelial layer
part_metadata.description: Thin supporting connective tissue beneath the endothelium. Support and lining are distinct tissue roles in the intima. The separation and relief are schematic; no universal internal elastic lamina is inferred. Directional support relief is schematic, not a fibre-by-fibre microstructural reconstruction.

part_metadata.name: Venous valve connective tissue cores
part_metadata.description: Supporting connective-tissue cores of two pocket-like intimal folds. Their attached roots remain in the wall and free margins face heartward (-x). Rear pocket mouths face downstream. This is a nearly closed static teaching pose; no flow patency, competence or pathology is established. Directional support relief is schematic, not a fibre-by-fibre microstructural reconstruction.

part_metadata.name: Venous valve cusps
part_metadata.description: Endothelial covering of the two valve folds, enclosing their cores over both faces and free margins and continuing into the vein lining at the roots. Hide the covering to inspect support in place. Thickness and surface organization are teaching enlargements, with no pressure-driven valve cycle.

part_metadata.name: Tunica media (smooth muscle)
part_metadata.description: Relatively thin venous smooth-muscle media with connective support. Muscle tone contributes to regional venous capacitance, while systemic veins and venules together provide a major blood-volume reservoir. This static segment does not quantify volume storage, compliance or contraction. Coded cell/nuclear cues are shallow surface relief, not measured cellular or nuclear volumes.

part_metadata.name: Tunica adventitia
part_metadata.description: Outer connective supporting environment containing representative collagen, longitudinal muscle, wall-supply vessels, nerves and adipocytes. It blends toward surrounding connective tissue; the cropped specimen boundary is a teaching cut.

part_metadata.name: Longitudinal smooth muscle bundles
part_metadata.description: Longitudinal adventitial muscle samples in the supporting matrix. Development varies across venous regions; six representatives in the preserved draft are schematic samples, not a physiological count. This valved composite is not a vena cava specimen. Coded cell/nuclear cues are shallow surface relief, not measured cellular or nuclear volumes.

part_metadata.name: Adventitial collagen bundles
part_metadata.description: Fibrous support samples associated with the adventitial matrix. They contribute to wall support and attachment to surrounding tissue. Fibre organization is enlarged and sparse; no collagen recruitment, distension limit or suture test is measured.

part_metadata.name: Vasa vasorum
part_metadata.description: Enlarged representatives of vessels supplying the vein wall within or beside its adventitia. Real circulation includes exchange vessels and venous drainage. This named red part does not display a complete capillary and drainage network or certify lumen continuity or perfusion.

part_metadata.name: Nervi vasorum
part_metadata.description: Representative autonomic nerve courses in the adventitial environment near vascular muscle. Sympathetic activity can modulate regional venous capacitance. Neurotransmitter release, receptor action and contraction are not modeled; colored proximity does not certify a neuroeffector junction.

part_metadata.name: Perivascular fat
part_metadata.description: Enlarged adipocyte samples at the outer connective environment of the vein. Their number and size are teaching conventions. Static appearance does not establish endocrine activity, inflammation or disease.

part_metadata.name: Red blood cells
part_metadata.description: Sparse enlarged biconcave blood-cell examples in the main lumen and near valve pockets. They identify blood as context; spacing does not indicate hematocrit, physiological occupancy, trapped blood, sinus residence time or thrombosis.

part_metadata.name: Rolling leukocyte
part_metadata.description: Enlarged static leukocyte example near the endothelial lining. The retained source name is a stable selection key, not evidence of rolling. Recruitment commonly involves tethering/rolling, activation, firm adhesion and transmigration in postcapillary venules; none of those dynamic or molecular steps is demonstrated here.

summary: Representative schematic valved medium-vein segment showing a thin media, wider adventitial support and two pocket-like intimal folds. Longitudinal muscle and microstructures are selected teaching examples, not universal venous anatomy.
scale_note: Representative schematic valved medium-vein segment; nominal lumen diameter 4.48 mm and whole-specimen calibration 4 mm per model unit. The paired cusps are in a nearly closed static teaching pose, with pocket mouths facing heartward (-x). Six longitudinal adventitial muscle representatives are a selected sample, not a physiological count. Endothelial/valve coat thickness, tissue relief, microvessels, nerves, adipocytes and blood cells are enlarged display geometry; the native ruler does not certify their biological dimensions. The cropped sinus is not a patient morphometric measurement. Not every vein has valves, and this is not a vena cava specimen.

01 Wall overview.name: 01 Wall overview
01 Wall overview.note: Opaque wall context; enlarged blood examples suppressed. Heartward is -x. Corner cut is a teaching specimen cut. The static near-closed pose is not a diagnosis.

02 Enlarged cells shown.name: 02 Enlarged cells shown
02 Enlarged cells shown.note: Same camera and whole-wall scale as 01. Blood examples are enlarged symbols; their count/placement do not describe physiological flow or density.

03 Intimal fold.name: 03 Intimal fold
03 Intimal fold.note: Heartward is -x. Trace the intimal fold into its attached root and heartward-facing free margin; pocket mouths open downstream. Nearly closed static teaching pose; pressure-loaded opening/closure and valve competence are untested.

04 Cusp core revealed.name: 04 Cusp core revealed
04 Cusp core revealed.note: Covering hidden only for teaching: supporting core remains in place. Restore the endothelial covering to compare the fold with the adjacent lining. No physiological tissue removal or valve motion occurs.

05 Lining and support.name: 05 Lining and support
05 Lining and support.note: Inspect the thin cellular lining and its underlying support in their correct layer order.

06 Media orientation.name: 06 Media orientation
06 Media orientation.note: Thin venous media illustrates muscular wall organization. Capacitance is volume at a given distending pressure; compliance is volume change per pressure change. No pressure-volume curve or wall contraction is modeled.

07 Adventitial context.name: 07 Adventitial context
07 Adventitial context.note: Keep connective context when relating collagen, longitudinal muscle, wall vessels, nerves and fat. Individual teaching samples are enlarged and sparse; they are not free-standing rods in life.

08 Muscle in support.name: 08 Muscle in support
08 Muscle in support.note: Longitudinal adventitial muscle is region-dependent. Six draft samples preserve source orientation; this valved teaching composite is not a vena cava specimen or a universal venous-wall formula.

09 Wall microvessels.name: 09 Wall microvessels
09 Wall microvessels.note: Enlarged wall-supply representatives, separate from main-lumen blood. Real wall circulation includes capillary exchange and venous drainage; this red part does not display a complete perfused circuit. Specimen exits are crops, not blind physiological endings.

10 Nerves and muscle.name: 10 Nerves and muscle
10 Nerves and muscle.note: Sympathetic venous tone can lower capacitance in regional reservoirs and recruit stressed volume. Signals, receptors and muscle contraction are narrated, not animated or quantified by this local model.

11 Fat boundary.name: 11 Fat boundary
11 Fat boundary.note: Adipocyte samples belong to the outer connective environment. Cell size and counts are schematic. Endocrine signaling or inflammatory state cannot be read from these static samples.

12 Cell contact.name: 12 Cell contact
12 Cell contact.note: Enlarged leukocyte example near the lining. Rolling, adhesion and transmigration are not demonstrated. Recruitment chiefly occurs in postcapillary venules; a stationary cell does not establish it in this valved segment.

13 Assembled specimen.name: 13 Assembled specimen
13 Assembled specimen.note: Return Separate layers to zero and Tissue opacity to 100%. Compare deliberate specimen boundaries with true tissue continuity; an exterior view does not verify an open lumen or complete vessel network.

14 Valve end-on.name: 14 Valve end-on
14 Valve end-on.note: Heartward is -x. Nearly closed source pose remains static. Physiological closure need not require through-valve reverse flow, and forward-flow recirculation can wash sinus pockets. Geometry here does not certify patency, reflux or disease.

native_ui_actions.progression: Page Down/Page Up or Views menu uses existing camera control. For deterministic full reset use native_teaching.apply_view(model_view, camera_name).
native_ui_actions.limits: Native camera records reset hidden/forced/isolation, assembled reveal and sections; they do not reset group toggles, Tissue opacity or procedural Separate layers. apply_view uses show_all and existing sliders to restore those controls.

camera_basis: Authored x-axis sweep from -1 to +1; valve stations .085..49; approximate valve target x=-.44; leukocyte station .78 gives x=.56 on the authored negative-y/-z side. Positions are drafted from source parameters, not fitted to generated meshes.
deferred_checks: Actual native opening at 100% tissue opacity and zero procedural separation
Exact 13 names/groups/colors in serialized artifact and native viewer
Camera framing after final warp and refined tissue relief
Coating continuity and rooted core identity in both retained sides of native sections
Sections and selective hiding preserve readable native tissue boundaries
No color-only tissue distinction or false literal scale reading
